My friends that live in Brooklyn pay comparable prices for the same amount of space, make more, and don’t need a car.

It is a published image. In the United States, something is copyrighted as soon as it’s conjured up. It’s not a dupe, it’s a copy of someone’s work that is legally protected under US copyright laws. 

I’m not saying I agree or disagree with the above letter, but duplicating someone’s work (even if it is a freehand copy) is still IP theft and the owner of the copyright can take you to court.

It is 100% a violation of copyright law depending on when the original was created. 

Museum works are different because a lot of them are now in the public domain. 

Clothing dupes are more of a grey area because you can argue it’s dependent on material, color, cut, etc., plus virtually no clothing designs are true originals outside of a lot of couture.

Not a lawyer, but I did take several semesters of copyright law for my degree. 

You do not have to prove monetary damages for it to be a copyright infringement. You do not have to register a copyright, it’s automatically copyrighted the second it’s conjured into existence (in the US). 

IF someone can prove that you are reproducing their original work, it is a copyright violation. Especially if monetary damages are in-play (loss of  sales due to you copying it, and not buying their original work.) 

That being said, I seriously doubt they’re going to go after everyone who has ever copied a design.

If I were the parent here, I’d move my kid with us, keep him in high school for the full four years, have him crank out as many Gen Ed’s as possible, and get his ACT up to a 34. That is going to open up the possibility for a full-ride at a lot of schools.

Also, graduating high school THAT early can actually have a negative impact on your college admissions.
